claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supportable on an aggregate-readiness-and-monitoring theory despite a known performance gap in a named regulated-customer segment.
decision_criteria: A material weakness affecting a contractual customer segment or named launch use case must be treated as material regardless of product's low-volume or non-core characterization.
Certification is compliant only if the material limitation is resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Open legal review does not satisfy the policy threshold for certification.
General public guidance may support monitoring and documentation practices but cannot replace unmet internal policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Produce the final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed before launch.
Produce an approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case if certification is to proceed without resolution.
Produce the actual disclosure artifact or launch documentation showing the material limitation has been disclosed as required by policy.
Produce the governing launch-use-case or customer-commitment record showing whether the affected segment is in scope for certification.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the health-plan benefits support segment misses target and is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which makes the weakness material under the policy text.
